preamble: Insertion of [g] occurs in two settings. In Khalkha Mongolian, -g- appears between a stem ending in a long vowel or diphthong and a vowel-initial case suffix, which resolves hiatus (boroo 'rain' > boroogoor 'with rain'). In many nonstandard varieties of Spanish, a velar stop is inserted before word-initial [w], so huevo 'egg' is pronounced [ˈɡweβo], written güevo.

examples.note: Epenthetic -g- separates the long-vowel stem from the vowel-initial suffix.
After the diphthong -g- is inserted; the consonant-final plural stem takes the bare suffix (цайнуудаар cainuudaar).
Dialectal velar prothesis before the initial glide, written ⟨gü⟩ in eye-dialect spelling.
Listed by Wiktionary as a dialectal variant; vueso /ˈbweso/ shows the competing labial reinforcement.
